conclusion: No supported queue-only purge with durable completion was found in the inspected pinned API surface. This is a bounded source/API review, not a proof that no workaround could ever be built.

cause_vs_binding.claim: Android setup and all used static methods reach the same shared core instance; no binding mismatch found.
Completed app chain persists deny, calls optOut, then optOut/reset/optOut/close; the APIs used do not perform outbound queue deletion.
optOut changes capture gating/integrations; reset changes identity/preferences and preserves queued outbound events.

close schedules flush before disabling and stopping timers/network callbacks; queue flush and batch HTTP path have no optOut check. Existing queued work may therefore send while opted out if network permits.

beforeSend runs during capture before queue insertion. Disk reload decodes and submits the stored event without rerunning that hook; adding a consent check there alone cannot revoke already persisted events.

supported_purge_challenge.internal_clear: PostHogQueueInterface.clear is explicitly not public supported API; the config queueProvider, storagePrefix, httpClient, networkStatus and persistOptOut are marked PostHogInternal. The queue field is protected.
supported_purge_challenge.internal_clear_limit: Queue.clear only schedules dropAllRecords, exposes no completion result and does not first load cached files. It does not establish interrupted/durable purge or cancel already decoded/in-flight work.
supported_purge_challenge.public_encryption_counterargument: Encryption is a real public hook. Decrypt failure can cause unreadable files to be deleted, but no supported key-revocation/cancellation/durable-purge contract is exposed. Already decoded records may still be sent. No custom crypto or workaround implemented.
other_non_solutions: resetSharedInstance is testing-only and not deletion
maxQueueSize zero coerces to at least one
Changing SDK storage paths or directly deleting internal queue files would rely on internal behavior

measured_existing_run.ordering: offline capture20 -> completed revoke callback -> completed refused capture10 -> force-stop/relaunch -> deny observed -> offline new consent -> capture10 -> reconnect -> old20 and new10 arrive
measured_existing_run.meaning: Existing raw receipts demonstrate failed suppression after completed revocation; they do not show purge internals or an interruption during revocation.

app_gaps: Memory deny is followed by awaited preference write before native optOut
No persisted revocation_pending or generation barrier blocks regrant until cleanup completes
If stopped before durable deny, startup can read the old true preference and auto setup/grant
After persisted deny but incomplete cleanup, startup remains denied but a later grant can reopen surviving events
sdk_durability_limits: Android SDK optOut/reset preferences use SharedPreferences.apply with no durable acknowledgement exposed
close catches Throwable internally; MethodChannel success and app sdk=false do not attest successful teardown or purge
interrupted_revocation.acceptance: Define accepted revocation only after a durable deny/pending record. Deterministic crash points must cover before/after that record, between native operations and before completion acknowledgement. Restart online must remain fail-closed until cleanup is durably completed; then new events work, forbidden events never appear in any receiver window, and unrelated sentinels survive.
interrupted_revocation.pre_acceptance_limit: A process death before any durable record cannot truthfully be reported as an accepted revocation. Stronger immediate-from-request guarantees need an explicit recovery policy, not an optimistic PASS.

decision: Keep PostHog adoption blocked for the requested revocation guarantee; use the authorized fallback comparison rather than further speculative reset/close, internal-file, internal-API or crypto experiments.
limits: Vendor extraction contains 18 selected files, including the full core API dump; not an exhaustive review of all platforms or future releases
Vendor/spec tag and blob provenance are supplied and verified by the parent; this review reads that exact local material
Online post-optOut send possibility is a code-derived risk, not a newly executed native result
No SDK/lab changes, no runtime experiments, no external actions performed
